docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The Gītagovinda of Jayadeva, poet at the court of Lakṣmaṇasena of Bengal in the twelfth century and associated by tradition with Puri in Odisha: the estrangement and reunion of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in twelve cantos, each named after an aspect of Kṛṣṇa, with songs (aṣṭapadī) set to named rāgas and tālas. It has been sung in the temple of Jagannātha and in the music and dance of eastern and southern India ever since.
